court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: Final agency action reviewable
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Plan and master permits are final agency actions subject to judicial review.

issues.label: Plaintiff Article III standing
issues.why: Court must confirm injury, causation, and redressability for Friends of Animals based on challenged approvals.

issues.label: Organizational standing theory
issues.why: Court must assess whether the organization has standing via members, diversion of resources, or informational injury.

issues.label: Ripeness of claims
issues.why: Court must decide whether challenges are fit for review now or depend on future certificates/permits.

issues.label: Mootness and ongoing effects
issues.why: Court must assess whether any permit terms expired, changed, or were superseded, affecting live controversy.

issues.label: Statute of limitations timing
issues.why: Court must verify the petition was filed within APA limitations periods for each agency action.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: Court must decide whether any required administrative steps (comments/appeals) were prerequisites to suit.

issues.label: Venue and jurisdiction basis
issues.why: Court must ensure proper subject-matter jurisdiction (APA/ESA/NEPA) and proper venue.

issues.label: Scope of review record
issues.why: Court must define the administrative record and whether extra-record evidence is permissible.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply APA arbitrary-and-capricious/contrary-to-law review and any deference to agency expertise.

issues.label: Claims cause of action
issues.why: Court must identify whether ESA claims proceed under APA review or ESA citizen-suit provisions and the implications.

issues.label: Proper defendants/sovereign immunity
issues.why: Court must confirm waiver of sovereign immunity and that the Service/officials are proper parties.

issues.label: Remedy authority and form
issues.why: Court must determine whether to vacate permits, remand without vacatur, or order supplemental NEPA/ESA analyses.

issues.label: Severability of Plan vs permits
issues.why: Court must decide if flaws require setting aside the whole Plan, specific permits, or discrete provisions.

issues.label: ESA incidental take permit criteria
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Service satisfied each statutory prerequisite under 16 U.S.C. §1539(a)(2).

issues.label: Adequate conservation plan content
issues.why: Court must assess whether the submitted Plan includes required minimization/mitigation, funding, monitoring, and alternatives.

issues.label: Maximum extent practicable mitigation
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether minimization and mitigation were to the maximum extent practicable for covered activities.

issues.label: Mitigation proportionality/offsets
issues.why: Court must assess whether mitigation truly “fully offsets” or otherwise adequately compensates for projected take.

issues.label: Funding assurances reliability
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether Utah/developer fees legally and practically assure sufficient funding over ten years.

issues.label: No appreciable reduction finding
issues.why: Court must determine whether projected take and habitat loss appreciably reduce survival and recovery likelihood.

issues.label: Recovery vs survival emphasis
issues.why: Court must ensure the agency analyzed impacts on recovery, not merely short-term survival.

issues.label: Use of recovery units
issues.why: Court must decide whether defining and relying on three recovery units was lawful and scientifically supported.

issues.label: Geographic scope of permits
issues.why: Court must assess whether seven-county coverage and county-level master permits fit ESA authorization limits.

issues.label: Master permit legality
issues.why: Court must decide whether issuing permits to counties with downstream “certificates of inclusion” complies with ESA permitting scheme.

issues.label: Delegation/subdelegation concerns
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether allowing counties to administer certificates unlawfully subdelegates federal permitting authority.

issues.label: Certificate inclusion safeguards
issues.why: Court must assess whether later certificates have enforceable conditions, oversight, and public accountability.

issues.label: Covered activities definition
issues.why: Court must ensure the Plan clearly defines covered development actions and their take mechanisms.

issues.label: Take estimate methodology
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the 7,152 take projection is supported by data and rational assumptions.

issues.label: Habitat loss projections reasonableness
issues.why: Court must assess use of historical averages, treatment of growth, and whether underestimation renders analysis arbitrary.

issues.label: Fivefold scenario adequacy
issues.why: Court must decide whether considering a fivefold increase sufficiently addresses foreseeable higher development or is too speculative.

issues.label: Major/minor designation validity
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether area designations reflect rational criteria and best available information.

issues.label: Non-federal land limitation
issues.why: Court must confirm that Plan’s focus on non-federal lands matches ESA permitting authority and actual impacts.

issues.label: Low-quality habitat treatment
issues.why: Court must assess whether allowing take/translocation on low-quality habitat is consistent with recovery needs.

issues.label: Translocation effectiveness evidence
issues.why: Court must determine whether record supports translocation success rates and whether uncertainty was properly addressed.

issues.label: Mitigation timing and lag
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether mitigation occurs before/at time of take and whether temporal lag undermines offsets.

issues.label: Permanent protection measures
issues.why: Court must assess whether conservation banks/easements/acquisitions are durable, enforceable, and sufficient in quantity/quality.

issues.label: Site selection for mitigation
issues.why: Court must decide if mitigation site criteria ensure biologically meaningful replacement habitat and connectivity.

issues.label: Monitoring and adaptive management
issues.why: Court must assess whether monitoring, triggers, and enforceable adaptive measures are adequate, not discretionary.

issues.label: Enforcement mechanisms
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether permit conditions are enforceable against counties/developers and what happens upon noncompliance.

issues.label: Permit duration and review
issues.why: Court must assess whether a ten-year streamlining structure includes lawful reopener/adjustment provisions.

issues.label: Changed circumstances handling
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Plan addresses foreseeable changed circumstances (growth, disease) and provides responses.

issues.label: Unforeseen circumstances standard
issues.why: Court must assess compliance with ESA/HCP regulations on unforeseen circumstances and permittee assurances.

issues.label: Cumulative impacts within units
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether aggregated takes across counties/years were analyzed cumulatively, not piecemeal.

issues.label: Interspecific/ecosystem effects
issues.why: Court must consider whether the Service ignored important ecological relationships affecting prairie dog conservation.

issues.label: Disease risk consideration
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether disease (a known historical driver) was adequately incorporated in impacts and mitigation.

issues.label: Genetic diversity considerations
issues.why: Court must assess whether translocations and habitat fragmentation effects on genetic health were considered.

issues.label: Climate and drought effects
issues.why: Court must decide whether foreseeable climate-related habitat stress was an “important aspect of the problem” ignored.

issues.label: Jeopardy vs 10(a) standard
issues.why: Court must ensure the Service applied the correct 10(a) “no appreciable reduction” test and not an inapposite jeopardy framing.

issues.label: Section 7 consultation required
issues.why: Court must determine whether issuing the permits/Plan is a federal action requiring §7 consultation.

issues.label: Biological opinion adequacy
issues.why: If §7 applies, court must assess whether any BiOp/consultation properly analyzed effects and included an ITS as needed.

issues.label: Incidental take statement interplay
issues.why: Court must consider whether permit-authorized take interacts with any §7 incidental take statement requirements/limits.

issues.label: Species status reliance
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether threatened status and any 4(d) rule were correctly accounted for in take prohibitions and permits.

issues.label: 4(d) rule consistency
issues.why: Court must assess whether permit scheme aligns with any special rules governing take of this threatened species.

issues.label: NEPA applicability to permits
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Plan and master permits are major federal actions triggering NEPA review.

issues.label: NEPA document type proper
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether a FONSI/EA was adequate or whether an EIS was required.

issues.label: Hard look at environmental impacts
issues.why: Court must determine whether NEPA analysis took a hard look at habitat loss, translocation harms, and long-term effects.

issues.label: Significance determination validity
issues.why: Court must review whether finding “no significant impact” was rational given scale, uncertainty, and controversy.

issues.label: NEPA segmentation concerns
issues.why: Court must assess whether using master permits/certificates improperly segments analysis of site-specific development impacts.

issues.label: NEPA tiering and supplementation
issues.why: Court must decide whether later site-specific NEPA is required and whether supplementation triggers are defined.

issues.label: Reasonable alternatives analysis
issues.why: Court must assess whether NEPA considered a reasonable range of alternatives (different mitigation, limits, denial).

issues.label: No-action alternative
issues.why: Court must ensure NEPA included and evaluated a genuine no-action baseline.

issues.label: Baseline conditions accuracy
issues.why: Court must assess whether NEPA baseline for prairie dog populations/habitat was accurate and not misleading.

issues.label: Cumulative impacts under NEPA
issues.why: Court must determine whether NEPA adequately analyzed cumulative impacts with other development and conservation actions.

issues.label: Indirect effects analysis
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether indirect effects like induced growth, fragmentation, and predation changes were considered.

issues.label: Scientific integrity of NEPA
issues.why: Court must assess whether the agency disclosed data gaps/uncertainty and used high-quality information.

issues.label: Public participation adequacy
issues.why: Court must determine whether NEPA/ESA processes provided proper notice, comment opportunity, and responses to significant comments.

issues.label: Consideration of expert controversy
issues.why: Court must assess whether substantial scientific disputes about translocation/mitigation required deeper NEPA analysis or EIS.

issues.label: Mitigation reliance for FONSI
issues.why: Court must decide whether the agency’s mitigation commitments were sufficiently specific, enforceable, and likely to succeed to support a FONSI.

issues.label: Interagency/tribal consultation
issues.why: Court must consider whether required coordination (e.g., with state, tribes) occurred where mandated by law or regulation.

issues.label: Consistency with recovery plan
issues.why: Court must assess whether actions align with any existing species recovery plan and whether deviations were explained.

issues.label: Arbitrary treatment of uncertainties
issues.why: Court must decide whether acknowledged uncertainty (future development higher than average) was reasonably bounded and addressed.

issues.label: Administrative procedure compliance
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether required procedural steps for issuing HCP-based permits were followed (findings, documentation, publication).

issues.label: Permit conditions clarity
issues.why: Court must ensure permits include clear take limits, monitoring, reporting, and mitigation obligations.

issues.label: Intra-county allocation of take
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Plan lawfully allocates take among projects and prevents exceeding overall authorized take.

issues.label: Overtake consequences
issues.why: Court must determine whether mechanisms exist to halt/adjust authorizations if take exceeds projections.

issues.label: Federalism/state role limits
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether state/county roles remain within ESA’s federal framework and do not undermine federal protection.

issues.label: Equitable considerations in remedy
issues.why: Court must consider reliance interests (schools/hospitals) when deciding vacatur vs remand without vacatur, consistent with law.
